1.explanation:
1. We create a small HTML page (`test.html`) that includes a `<link>` and `<script>` pointing at a `file:///` URL, which on a real browser would never load but will still show up to Lighthouse’s parser.  
2. We spin up a minimal local HTTP server to serve that HTML so Lighthouse can navigate to it over `http://localhost:8080`.  
3. We programmatically launch a headless Chrome instance via `chrome-launcher`, invoke Lighthouse against our test page, and print out the `render-blocking-resources` audit details.  You will see the `file:///some/local/...` URL in the list with non-zero wasted milliseconds, demonstrating the bug.  
4. Finally, we clean up both the server and the Chrome process.
1.bug_scenario: A simple HTTP-served HTML page references a resource via the file:/// protocol (for example, a stylesheet or script on the local file system). When Lighthouse audits this page, it incorrectly flags the file:/// URL as a render-blocking resource under “Eliminate render-blocking resources,” even though local file:// requests never reach the network and cannot block rendering.
